claims: The 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified in 1967.
Section 1 of the 25th Amendment explicitly states that if the President dies, resigns, or is removed, the Vice President becomes President.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to nominate a Vice President if a vacancy occurs, subject to congressional approval.
Section 3 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to temporarily transfer power to the Vice President (Acting President) if they cannot fulfill duties.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment empowers the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to declare the President incapacitated and remove them from power.
An article from Congress.gov notes that Section 1 was used in 1974 when Gerald Ford became president following Richard Nixon's resignation.
Section 3 has been used multiple times.
Section 3 has been used during presidential surgeries.
Section 4 has never been invoked to permanently remove a president, according to Newsweek.
Section 4 requires a two-thirds vote in both houses of Congress if the president contests it, according to Newsweek.

The 25th Amendment was created to address ambiguities regarding presidential disability, particularly following the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, according to the Gerald R. Ford Presidential Library & Museum.
